la:noun:lapsus.html:
lapsus, ūs, m.
1. labor
,
a falling, fall; a slipping, sliding, gliding, running, flowing, flying, flight, etc. (class.).
Lit.: ac celeri ferme percurrunt fulmina lapsu,: atque ea, quae lapsu tandem cecidere vetusto, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 11, 19: infrenis equi lapsu jacens,: tum quassao nutant turres, lapsumque minantur,: horrere lapsus tectorum assiduos,.—Of a landslide: locus recenti lapsu terrae abruptus,: lapsu scalarum exanimatus,by falling down stairs,: ut neque sustinere se a lapsu possent,: puerilium dentium,the shedding,: si lacus emissus lapsu et cursu suo ad mare profluxisset,: (stellae) certo lapsu spatioque feruntur,course,; cf.: medio volvuntur sidera lapsu,: molli zephyros descendere lapsu adspiciunt,: accepere deae, celerique per aethera lapsu, periere, etc.,: volucrum lapsus,flight,; cf.: facili lapsu ad deos pervolare, id. Fragm. ap. (19), 6: gemini lapsu delubra ad summa dracones Effugiunt,: vitis serpens multiplici lapsu et erratico,: rotarum,i. e. rolling wheels, (cf. τροχῶν βάσεις, Soph. Elect. 718; and remigium alarum = alae,): arte materna rapidos morantem Fluminum

lapsus, i. e. flumina, . —

Transf., of the effects of a fall; in plur.: contra ulcera, rupta, lapsusque, bruises, contusions received in falling, .—
Trop., a failing, error, fault (rare but class.): amor lapsum animi ludificat,: ab omni lapsu continere temeritatem,to restrain one's rashness in believing from leading him into error,: cum sint populares multi variique lapsus,of losing popularity,: haud alius fidei pronior lapsus, quam ubi, etc.,.

la:noun:lapis.html:
lăpis, ĭdis (abl. lapi, Enn. ap. P.;
gen. plur. lapiderum, C. Gell. ap. P.), m. (f.: tanto sublatae sunt augmine tunc lapides, Enn. ap. ) [etym. dub.; perh. from same root with rupes; cf. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 545; not connected with λᾶας, ], a stone (cf.: saxum, silex, cautes, cos, calculus).
In gen.: stillicidi casus lapidem cavat,: undique lapides in murum jaci coepti sunt,; cf. : pars eminus glande aut lapidibus pugnare,: lapide percussus,: lapidem habere, ut illi cerebrum excutiam,; cf. : consul ingentem vim modicorum, qui funda mitti possent, lapidum paraverat,; sqq.: e lapide duro parietes construere,: lapis duritia marmoris,: bibulus,sandstone, pumice-stone,: molaris,a millstone,; cf.: num me illue ducis, ubi lapis lapidem terit?i. e. into the mill,: Parius, Parian stone, i. e. Parian marble, : lapide candidiore diem notare,i. e. to mark with a white stone the luckiest day,; cf. lapillus.—
Trop. for dulness, stupidity, want of feeling: ego me credidi homini docto rem mandare: is lapidi mando maximo,: i, quid stas, lapis? quin accipis?; cf. : tu, inquam, mulier, quae me omnino lapidem, non hominem putas,; and with silex (q. v.): tu es lapide silice stultior,; cf.: lapides mehercule omnes flere ac lamentari coëgisses,: lapis est ferrumque suam quicumque puellam verberat,: aut mare prospiciens in saxo frigida sedi, quamque lapis sedes, tam lapis ipsa fui,.—Prov.: lapidem ferre altera manu, altera panem ostentare,i. e. to flatter openly and injure secretly,: verberare lapidem,i. e. to hurt one's self more than one's enemy,: lapides loqui,to speak hard words,: ad eundem lapidem bis offendere,to commit the same error twice,; so, bis ad eundem (sc. lapidem),.—
In partic.
A mile-stone, set up on the roads at every thousand paces, which made a Roman mile; hence, with an ordinal numeral added to denote distance in miles: ad quartum et vicesimum lapidem a Roma,; cf.: effoditur ad vigesimum ab Urbe lapidem,: sacra videt fieri sextus ab Urbe lapis,: intra vicesimum lapidem,: duodecimum apud lapidem,: a tertio lapide,: ad lapidem undecimum, Paul. ex Müll.—Sometimes ellipt. without lapis: ad duodecimum a Cremona,: ad quartum,: ad octavum,.—
The stone or stone elevation on which the prætor stood at slavesales: in eo ipso astas lapide, ubi praeco praedicat,; : praeter duos de lapide emptos tribunos,.—
Terminalis, a landmark, boundary-stone, ; called lapis alone,; so, lapis sacer,; cf.: non fixus in agris, qui regeret certis finibus arva, lapis,; cf. .—
A gravestone, tombstone, ; ; called also ultimus,.—
A precious stone, gem, jewel, pearl (mostly poet.), : gemmas et lapides,: clari lapides,; ; ; ; ; .—
A statue: Jovem lapidem jurare, the statue of Jupiter at the Capitol, ; ; v. Juppiter.—*
Meton.: albus,a table of white marble, a marble table,.

la:verb:lapido.html:
lăpĭdo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
lapis
,
to throw stones at a person or thing, to stone ( = lapidibus obruo, percutio; not ante-Aug.).
With personal object: exercitus imperatorem lapidavit,; : eum lapidare coeperunt, Auct. B. Hisp. 23: Stephanum,: Paulum,.—
To cast stones upon, to bury: praeteriens aliquis nos lapidabit,.—
With an inanim. object: quo defunctus est die, lapidata sunt templa,.—
Trop., to assail, assault, strike at: notantes impotentiam ejus hac dicacitate lapidatam,—
Impers.: lapidat, it rains stones: quia Veiis de caelo lapidaverat,: Reate imbri lapidavit,.—In the pass. form: quod de caelo lapidatum esset,: propter crebrius eo anno de caelo lapidatum,.

la:verb:lapso.html:
lapso, āre,

Lit. (poet. and in postAug. prose): (Priamum) in multo lapsantem sanguine nati,: sanguine suo et lubrico paludum lapsantes (equi),: lapsantibus equis,: lapsantem gressum firmare,; : Gyan vidi lapsare cruentae Vulnere Myrmidonis,fall,: plantis lapsantibus,.—
Trop. (post-class.): verba lapsantia,i. e. babbled forth,.

la:noun:lapillus.html:
lăpillus, i, m.dim.
lapis
,
a little stone, a pebble (perh. not ante-Aug.).
In gen.: invitat somnos crepitantibus unda lapillis,; —Lucky days were marked with white, and unlucky ones with black stones (cf. calculus, 2. e.); hence: felix utraque lux diesque nobis Signandi melioribus lapillis,i. e. with white stones,; cf.: hunc Macrine, diem numera meliore lapillo,; cf. also . —In trials at law, a white stone was cast as a vote for acquittal, a black stone for condemnation: mos erat antiquus niveis atrisque lapillis, His damnare reos, illis absolvere culpa,.—
In partic.
Stone in the bladder, gravel: ejectus calculoso,.—
A precious stone, gem, jewel; marble, etc.: inter niveos viridesque lapillos, i. e. pearls andemeralds, : caris aures onerare lapillis,: indici,: Libyci,bits of Numidian marble,.—
A tombstone, Inscr. ap. Murat. 1536, 6; cf. Burm. Anth. Lat. 2, p. 269.

For lapidosus, full of stones, stony (post-Aug.): lapidei campi,; : litus,.
